subject: Clarify default log horizon and deletion for requests vs model outputs — BrightBank
messages:
From: Evan Liu <evan.liu@brightbank.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick Q on what you keep by default (requests vs outputs)

Laura —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our InfoSec reviewer followed up with a narrow question: in Redwood's hosted offering, what is the default "log horizon" for different artifact types? Specifically they want to know the default retention windows for: (a) raw request payloads (full user input), (b) model outputs/generation tokens, and (c) intermediate prompt artifacts (templated prompts, few-shot context). Also: what deletion/expunge paths do you provide if we request purging of a given user's data?

We don't need legalese yet — just the operational defaults so we can map to our policy. If possible include whether any items are kept for debugging longer, and what customers can configure.

Appreciate a short bulleted reply we can pass to the security team.

—Evan
BrightBank (Security)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Evan Liu <evan.liu@brightbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-09T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q on what you keep by default (requests vs outputs)

Evan —

Thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Marissa (product) and Kimberly (security) to give a crisp operational summary. Below is a short-form answer you can share; happy to expand into an annex or checklist.

- Default retention windows (hosted API):
  • Raw requests (user input): retained for 45 days by default.
  • Model outputs (generated text): retained for 45 days by default.
  • Prompt templates / few-shot context (customer-provided prompt artifacts): treated as request derivatives and retained for 45 days by default.

- Debugging exceptions: aggregated telemetry (traces, anonymized error logs) may be retained up to 90 days to support incident triage; raw request/response content is not kept longer unless a customer opts into extended retention.

- Purge path: customers can submit a data deletion request via Console -> Data & Privacy -> Request Delete (or via support ticket). Deletion flow: mark ➜ tombstone index ➜ background purge job (up to 72 hours) ➜ verification. For hosted customers we also clear caches and KV entries related to the request during purge.

- Configurability: enterprise customers can change default horizons (e.g., 0 days / immediate ephemeral, or custom retention periods), and Dedicated/Private deployments can be configured to never persist request/response artifacts unless explicitly enabled.

Marissa / Kimberly — please add anything I missed (SLA/annex wording, or items to call out for auditors).

Thanks,
Laura
Senior Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-10T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q on what you keep by default (requests vs outputs)

Evan —

Adding operational clarifications and a concrete example your auditor will like.

- Classification: we consider the following categories: request (entire inbound HTTP body including metadata), generated output (final tokens delivered to customer), and artifacts (prompt templates, system messages, few-shot examples). All three are treated as "customer artifacts" by default.

- Default retention rationale: 45 days balances customers' desire for incident/debugging window with privacy safeguards. Shorter windows (24–72 hours) are available for SOC-driven customers.

- Example timeline for a single user purge request:
  1) Customer initiates purge in Console or via support (Ticket created, ID recorded).
  2) Data is immediately removed from live serving indices (marked tombstoned).
  3) Background purge job removes objects from object store and invalidates caches within 72 hours.
  4) Audit log entry produced and returned to customer (Doc ID / timestamp).

- Edge notes: encrypted backups are rotated per backup policy (30/90/365 days depending on retention class). Purge requests initiate metadata cleanup for backup retention windows, but complete physical removal from backups may vary by backup retention class — we provide a customer-specific statement in the SLA annex.

I'll attach the standard retention annex for BrightBank to this thread.

—Marissa
Staff PM, Product Privacy
Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-08-12T10:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q on what you keep by default (requests vs outputs)

Quick technical clarifications (apologies for the detail but auditors like precise behavior):

- KV/prefix caching: live inference uses ephemeral KV caches for attention/key/value shards; these caches are in-memory and not persisted to long-term stores. When a request is completed the in-memory KV entries are eligible for eviction immediately; they are not part of the 45-day retention window.

- Streaming and partial outputs: intermediate streaming buffers are flushed to the response stream and then discarded. Only the final assembled output (what we show as "model output" in the Console) falls under the 45-day artifact retention.

- Auditability: deletion actions are recorded in an immutable audit log (entry contains ticket id, operator, timestamp). For hosted customers, we provide the audit log entry URL as confirmation of purge completion.

Let me know if you want a short one-page note for your auditor that lines this up with BrightBank policy language.

- Aditya
Senior SW Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
